content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 1 (as on 14.07.2025)
Key Insights

1. Kharif Sowing Status: As on 11 July, 2025, the area sown under Kharif crops is 597.86 lakh ha (including 55.16 lakh ha (105% of normal area) in Sugarcane) as compared to 560.59 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. About 54.5 percent of the normal area has been sown under the Kharif season crops. The status of sowing under Rice, Pulses and Coarse Cereals is better than in the same period of last year. 2. Weather Update: a) Temperature: Maximum temperatures is likely to be above normal Bihar, East U.P., many parts in NE India, some parts in South Karnataka, and coastal regions of Tamil Nadu and Coastal AP. b) Rainfall Distribution: From June 01– 13, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 10% higher than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: (-)24%; (ii) Northwest India: 30%; (iii) Central India: 37%; and South Peninsula:(-) 8%. A fresh Western Disturbance seen as a trough in middle tropospheric levels with roughly along Long. 62°E to the north of Lat. 30°N. Likely Formation of two Low pressure systems; one over northwest Madhya Pradesh and neighbourhood and another over northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining coastal areas of West Bengal and Odisha. Heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy likely over west Madhya Pradesh on 13th July, East Rajasthan during 13th to 15th July, West Rajasthan on 14th & 15th 2025. Heavy to very heavy rainfall likely over east India during next 2-3 days. Fairly widespread to widespread rainfall very likely over East, Northeast & South Peninsular India, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Islands. Isolated to Scattered rainfall very likely over rest parts of the country. Overall, Rainfall is likely to be above normal over Central India, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Odisha. 3. Inputs Situation a) Water Reservoir Status: As on 10th July 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 94.51 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 52% of total live storage capacity (182.46 BCM). The current year's storage is nearly 196 percent of last year's storage and 183 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.

content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 2 b) Groundwater Levels: Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 0-5 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014–2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024. c) Seeds and Fertilizers: For Kharif 2025, certified seed availability is 178.64 lakh quintals against a requirement of 164.05 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 14.60 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products. 4. Pests & Diseases: The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level (ETL) and no major pest incidence was recorded. 5. content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 3
Details of each Segment
1. RAINFALL

• During the week (03 July - 09 July2025), higher rainfall was observed, as compared to Long Period Average (LPA) by 26%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01th June to 09th July 2025) is higher than LPA by 15%. Rainfall Forecast: • Overall, near normal to above normal rainfall activity is likely over central India; near normal over most parts of northwest and south Peninsular India; below normal rainfall activity is likely over most parts of east & northeast India during the week. • The monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Bikaner, centre of low-pressure area over northwest Madhya Pradesh and adjoining east Rajasthan, Satna, Jamshedpur, centre of well-marked low pressure area over southwest Bangladesh and adjoining Gangetic West Bengal.

2. TEMPERATURE: MIN & MAX

Temerature Week 1 (11 July – 17 July2025): • Maximum temperatures are likely to be above normal by 2-4°C over Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and most parts of northeast India. These are likely to be below normal or near normal over rest parts of the country. Week 2 (18 July - 24 July 2025): • These are likely to be above normal by 2-3°C over many parts of east & northeast India and Uttar Pradesh. These are likely to be below normal or near normal over rest parts of the country.

content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 6
4. REMOTE SENSING BASED SOIL MOISTURE OBSERVATION

Soil Moisture Observation • Soil moisture as on 10 July 2025 was similar/better than the average of the past 9 years in major parts of Gujarat, Rajasthan, M.P, Maharashtra, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Southern West Bengal, Haryana and Western & Bundelkhand regions of U.P. • It was lower than average of past 9 years in Bihar, Eastern parts of U.P., Northern parts of West Bengal, Telangana, A.P., in parts of Karnataka and N.E. part of country.

5. CROP SOWING STATUS FOR KHARIF SEASON

Kharif Crops - Area coverage • Rice: About 123.68 lakh ha area coverage under Kharif Rice as compared to 111.85 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. • Soybean: About 99.03 lakh ha area coverage under Soyabean has been reported as compared to 107.78 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. • Sugarcane: About 55.16 lakh ha area coverage under Sugarcane has been reported as compared to 54.88 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. • Cotton: About 92.83 lakh ha area coverage has been reported compared to 95.22 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.
